_: The one source for estate memory in every agent runtime (#6156). bin/estate-memory-install renders this into each runtime's own config and --check reports drift. A new runtime is a new entry under runtimes, not a new integration.
mcp_reads: Whether a runtime can read an MCP server at all. pi cannot: its own docs say 'No MCP' -- there is no client to register one with, so the mcp entry below is dead config that reads like a working integration. 'reads': false tells the installer to leave that file alone and to remove the estate's own entry from it; a runtime with no MCP client gets its tools from the 'tools' links instead, which point at the same bridge every other runtime runs.
plan_lock: How each runtime refuses work until a plan allows it (#6675): hook (the enforce plan hook above), plugin (the opencode hook file), extension (bin/pi-plan-lock-install). null means nothing enforces it there yet; such a runtime names its command, and the installer fails while that command is on PATH.
runtime_enforce: How a runtime reaches the write-side gates (the enforce bin above) when it has no hooks of its own. pi has no hook mechanism, so it gets an extension that renders pi's session into the transcript the binary reads and turns the binary's answer into pi's two refusals: the rules stay in the binary, so one rule decides for every runtime (#7006). A list, like 'tools'.
